heading: The week in short
body:
This was a quiet week with no big shocks. The 30th Celebration special illustration rares are still drifting down, but more slowly: Mew ex 152 is −6% against its 30-day average (it was −12% last week) at €79.66, Pikachu ex 150 is €47.83. Règne Delta is in Réunion at Miyata Kard Market: a second restock is due on 17 November, with the Elite Trainer Box at €79.99 and the 36-booster display at €239.99. In One Piece, OP-18 arrives on 20 November (English) and 21 November (Japanese), and sealed OP-17 is falling faster (−13% in four weeks) as it nears. We still cannot confirm any One Piece or Pokémon results after 31 October.

What to do: hold your 30th Celebration singles and buy any you still want slowly. If you want Règne Delta sealed, check Miyata after 17 November; do not pay launch prices for singles yet. Don't buy OP-17 boxes expecting a quick rebound.

heading: Règne Delta: first French prices on the island
body:
Miyata Kard Market lists French Règne Delta (ME06): single booster €7.99, three-pack €19.99, 6-booster bundle €44.99 (was €49.99), Elite Trainer Box €79.99 (was €89.99) and the 36-booster display €239.99. The page says a second wave arrives on 17 November. Most items show 'Épuisé' (sold out) today, and several show an add-to-cart button at the same time, so check each product page before you travel.

For comparison, one booster at €7.99 from the display works out at €6.67 (€239.99 ÷ 36). The display is the cheapest way per pack; the ETB is the cheapest way to get a nice box with 9 boosters.

Mega Rayquaza ex prices: we could not get a trustworthy number this week. TCGdex's Cardmarket feed still shows a €3.55–€4.20 placeholder for every Mega Rayquaza ex, which is clearly wrong, and the third-party dollar estimates from last week ($285–$400 for the SIR and gold card) were not re-checked. Treat those as last week's guesses.

heading: 30th Celebration: the slide is slowing
body:
Cardmarket data via TCGdex, read 16 November (7-day average against 30-day average): Mew ex 152 €79.66 (−6%), Pikachu ex 150 €47.83 (−4%), Mewtwo ex 151 €43.96 (−7%), Gengar ex 154 €61.80 (−6%), Jirachi ex 155 €30.36 (−8%), Greninja ex 148 €15.77 (−7%), Sylveon ex 153 €31.66 (−1%) and Salamence ex 156 €15.37 (−3%). Last week these were −7% to −14%, so the fall is flattening. Meowth 144 and Maushold 146 fell 17% but are around €4–5.

Mega Darkrai ex 116 (Pitch Black) is steady at €176.27, up from €169.56. Morpeko ex 117 is €46.94 (−8%).

Reading it simply: prices are still going down but more gently. A floor may be close. If you want one for the binder, buying one card now and one in two weeks is a sensible way to spread the risk.

heading: OP-18: English 20 November, Japan 21 November
body:
Bandai's English event page runs OP-18 release events from 20 November, and a guide citing the Japanese official page gives 21 November for Japan. Earlier reports of 22 or 28 November predate the official pages. We treat 20 and 21 November as very likely but the French date is still unconfirmed. Japan runs a release event from 21 November to 6 December. Cards become tournament legal seven days after release (a secondary source, Samurai Sword Tokyo).

Limitless now lists OP-18 as the set for Regionals from Alicante (28 November), then Munich, Utrecht, Santiago and Mexico City (5 December), and Paris (12 December).

Collector view: a new set pulls attention and money away from older boxes. See the next section.
source: Bandai (English event page); Samurai Sword Tokyo; Limitless

heading: Sealed boxes: OP-05 and OP-10 up, OP-17 and OP-09 down
body:
Japanese booster-box prices (eBay sold medians, opboxindex, 16 November): OP-05 $213 (+22% in four weeks), OP-10 $100 (+15%), OP-12 $120 (+4%), OP-17 $109 (−13%, last week −7%), OP-09 $109 (−23%), OP-02 $131 (−19%), OP-01 $261 (−13%). OP-07, OP-11, OP-15 and OP-16 are flat; EB-05 is $109.

Warning: EB-02 is shown at $159 (+18%), but last week the same site showed $100 and −26%. A swing like that in a week suggests thin sales, so don't trade on it.

Some of these prices are old. For example OP-02 was last sold on 24 October. A box that rarely sells can show an out-of-date median.

What to do: OP-17 is the one to watch. It is a recent set still falling before OP-18; buy it later, not now. OP-05 has momentum but it is already up 22%, so buying now is chasing.

heading: Championships: no new results to report
body:
Pokémon: Limitless lists nothing after Regional Gdańsk (31 October, won by Aarni Karjala with Slowking). Special Championships Buenos Aires ran 14–15 November (Serebii), but no winner has been published yet. The deck table is unchanged: Dragapult ex 36.5%, Basic Box 8.9%, Slowking 7.6%, N's Zoroark ex 7.3%, Alakazam 6.4%.

One Piece: Limitless's results page still ends on 26 July. We cannot confirm the 7 November Porto and Sydney Regionals or any 14 November events. The Bristol organiser page says Bristol is on 21–22 November (Ashton Gate), which conflicts with Limitless's list from last week. One Piece meta shares are last week's and unconfirmed.

Next: Latin America Internationals in São Paulo (20–22 November), Champions League Chiba (22 November) and Regional Stuttgart (28 November).
source: Limitless TCG; Serebii; Organized Play events

heading: Your collection
body:
Rebuilt on 16 November: 94 of 122 cards priced (last week 95), listed value about €61.56 (last week €65.24). The set priced is almost the same as last week, so this fall is real: about −6%. The main reason is Dragonite 149/165 (€5.84 to €4.33) and Dragonair 148/165 (€4.13 to €3.58). Rate used: Rs 52.53 per euro (last week 52.95).

Your top cards: Albia 109/084 €6.51, Flagadoss 090/084 €5.95, Arcanine 059/165 €4.41, Dragonite 149/165 €4.33, Hitmonlee 107/165 €4.06. Denticrisse 051/198 lost its price this week.

What to do: nothing to sell. At these amounts the whole collection is worth about the price of one Elite Trainer Box and a booster bundle. Dragonair 148/165 and Charizard ex 006/165 remain marked Rising, but we did not verify the label changes beyond the price data. Keep them.

heading: Language gaps
body:
We did not find new comparable English, French and Japanese prices this week. Cardmarket pools languages into one price, and TCGdex returns placeholder prices for Règne Delta.

The only gap we can show: a French booster at Miyata is €7.99 in Réunion. We have no matching Cardmarket booster price, so we cannot say whether that is cheap or expensive.

Last week's figures for the Mega Rayquaza gold card in Japan (¥50,000–84,800) and the OP-17 Manga D. Xebec (about ¥436,000 in Japan, about $6,100 in English) were not re-checked. Treat them as last week's.

heading: Your Réunion window: 41 days left
body:
You have 41 days on the island until 27 December. This week's tasks: (1) Miyata Kard Market in Saint-Louis, second Règne Delta wave on 17 November (ETB €79.99, display €239.99, bundle €44.99). (2) Ask Sortilèges, Planet Geek and PUNK Records about OP-18 French stock; Sortilèges' home page shows no products or prices, only that animation events are back in the shop and a pre-order notice. PUNK Records in Le Tampon is the One Piece specialist.

Buy the sealed French products you want before 27 December; after that you will be buying from Mauritius.

The exchange rate is now Rs 52.53 per euro (xe.com mid-market, 16 November; valutafx.com blocked the request).

heading: Coming up
body: 17 Nov: Miyata Règne Delta restock. 20 Nov: One Piece OP-18 (EN); Pokémon Latin America Internationals (to 22 Nov). 21 Nov: OP-18 Japan; Regional Oklahoma City (One Piece); Bristol Regionals (21–22 Nov per the organiser, unconfirmed). 22 Nov: Champions League Chiba. 27 Nov: Pokémon Aura Seeker in Japan (reported date). 28 Nov: Regional Stuttgart (Pokémon) and Regional Alicante (One Piece). 5 Dec: Pokémon Las Vegas; One Piece Munich, Utrecht, Santiago, Mexico City. 12 Dec: One Piece Paris. 18–19 Dec: One Piece ST-37 and ST-38. Early 2027: Valentine's Day box (27 Jan, reported), Aura Seeker in English as Flowing Fists (5 Feb, reported), M7a (19 Feb, unconfirmed).

heading: About the numbers
body: Euro prices come from Cardmarket via TCGdex (read 16 November); movers compare the 7-day with the 30-day average, and I only checked the 30th Celebration and Pitch Black cards plus a few Règne Delta cards. One Piece box prices are eBay sold medians in dollars from opboxindex, some dated more than two weeks ago. Unconfirmed: all results after 31 October (both games), Bristol's date, the French OP-18 date, Aura Seeker's date, the Mega Rayquaza prices and the EB-02 figure. The exchange rate (Rs 52.53) comes from xe.com. Collection: 94 of 122 cards priced (last week 95).
